task.name: Declarative typed issue specification: one contract the checker validates against, producers render through, and documentation is generated from
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2723
---

## Problem

There is no artifact that states what a well-formed issue is. `shape_check` embodies the
rules, every prose restatement of them has drifted, and no producer has a canonical form to
render against. ADR-0009 decides that a declarative specification becomes the contract; this
issue builds it.

## What

A per-type declarative specification, as data, covering canonical type label, section
headings and their order, which sections are required and which are forbidden, field-level
constraints, and lifecycle states. Alongside it, the parse and render halves that make the
specification usable: existing bodies parse into a typed document, and typed documents
render back to canonical Markdown.

The checker validates against the specification instead of restating it. Reference
documentation is generated from it.

## Why the current check cannot be repaired in place

The acceptance-criterion check this specification replaces is sensitive to line wrapping.
Bullets are truncated to their first line before the verb match runs, so a criterion whose
verb falls on a continuation line reads as having none. This issue's own criteria hit it:
one bullet ended `...emits only the canonical spelling`, `emits` is in the accepted set, and
the check still fired because the word sat on the second line.

Together with the closed 30-word vocabulary and its tense sensitivity — `writes` counts,
`written` does not — the check makes admission depend on word choice, verb tense and text
layout rather than on whether a reviewer could verify the outcome. It is retired here rather
than corrected, because each of those is a separate correction to a rule that should not be
structural at all.

## Why

Slice 3 of the typed-intake-contract epic, and the one every later slice needs. The
authoring front end compiles into it, producers render through it, and the documentation is
a rendering of it. Until it exists those are each free to invent their own idea of the
required parts, which is the situation today.

## Acceptance criteria

- A per-type specification exists as data and states, for each type, the canonical label,
  the section headings and their order, which sections are required and which are forbidden,
  and the lifecycle states the type can occupy.
- The checker derives its structural rules from the specification rather than carrying its
  own copy; a rule changed in the specification changes what the checker enforces with no
  second edit.
- Rendering a typed document emits only the canonical heading spelling, while both the
  canonical and the legacy spellings parse into the same typed document.
- Rendering a document parsed from an already-canonical body produces that body unchanged.
- Rendering writes back content the specification does not model, intact, rather than
  dropping it.
- CI fails when the generated reference documentation and the specification disagree, so a
  rule cannot be enforced without being documented.

## Example

The round trip that must hold, and does not today:

```
body_in  = canonical bug body, gate-passing
doc      = parse(body_in)            # typed IssueDocument
body_out = render(doc)

body_out == body_in                  # unchanged
```

#2053 is the observed failure of this property: `forge shape --apply` rewrote a
gate-passing bug body into one the gate refused.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the third-cycle P1: heading recognition was narrower than heading canonicalization. `## Reproduction` is a declared alias — the parser models it as the reproduction section and the renderer rewrites it to `## Steps to reproduce` — but the gate probed with the hand-written recognition_pattern, which matched only the canonical spelling, so a task or enhancement carrying that forbidden section was reported runnable. SectionSpec.heading_pattern now derives the probe regex by widening recognition_pattern with an anchored alternative for each declared alias the broad pattern does not already cover, and every heading probe in parsing.py, heuristics.py and intake/shape_render.py uses it. Declaring an alias is therefore the whole edit; the hand-written pattern stays broad on top of it, so `## Observed behavior` is still recognized as a symptom heading. All six modeled sections were swept for the same gap — only reproduction had one — and a property test now asserts the invariant for every section and alias so a future alias cannot reopen it.

plan_structured.approach: Introduce a stdlib-only typed issue contract module, then make parsing, rendering, validation, intake rewriting, and generated docs consume that single contract. Keep public entry points such as `shape_check.check()` and `intake.shape_render.restructure_body()` stable while replacing their private structural rule copies.

steps.description: Add the declarative per-type issue specification
steps.details: Define frozen pure-data records for issue types, sections, aliases, required/forbidden sections, field constraints, lifecycle states, and canonical labels. Fold the existing bug Diagnosis component data from `diagnosis_spec.py` into this contract or re-export it from the new contract so diagnosis labels remain one source of truth. Include the known typed labels: bug, enhancement, epic, task/documentation-style work, operator-action, adr-candidate, and duplicate-or-stale only where the current classifier/checker recognizes them.

steps.description: Add a typed issue document parser and renderer
steps.details: Create typed document records that preserve document order, raw section bodies, unmatched prose, and unknown sections. Reuse existing fence-aware heading parsing from `parsing.py`; extend only as needed so canonical and legacy heading aliases resolve to the same modeled section while unknown/unmodeled content is retained as passthrough. The renderer emits canonical type labels and canonical modeled headings, but preserves already-canonical raw content byte-for-byte on `render(parse(body))`.

steps.description: Retarget structural shape checks to the specification
steps.details: Keep `check(title, body, labels, ...)` as the external API, but parse the body into the typed document once and derive recognized labels, required sections, forbidden sections, lifecycle refusals, and section-order checks from `issue_spec.py`. Retire the closed acceptance-criteria observable-verb vocabulary as an admission rule; keep semantic warnings advisory-only if still useful. Preserve existing `ShapeResult` fields for compatibility while ensuring admission is driven by the spec-derived structural/lifecycle outcome.

steps.description: Make intake rendering use the typed renderer
steps.details: Keep `restructure_body()` and existing proposal rendering behavior, but build repaired bodies by parsing to the typed document, adding missing modeled sections or fields from the spec, and rendering through the canonical renderer. Ensure legacy headings parse but render as canonical headings, canonical inputs render unchanged, and unmodeled sections/prose are written back intact.

steps.description: Generate reference documentation from the issue specification
steps.details: Replace the narrow diagnosis-only reference generation with a spec renderer that emits the full per-type reference. Keep `docs/reference/bug-shape.md` if existing links depend on it, but make it generated from the same contract or reduce it to a generated bug-specific slice. Update the authoring guide to point at generated reference material instead of restating structural rules manually.

steps.description: Add contract, round-trip, checker, producer, and docs drift tests
steps.details: Add focused tests proving spec changes affect `check()` without a second rule edit, canonical and legacy headings parse to the same typed document, canonical bodies round-trip unchanged, unknown content survives rendering, `restructure_body()` no-ops on gate-passing canonical bodies, and generated docs exactly match the checked-in reference. Adjust old tests that assert the retired observable-verb admission behavior.
